name: Tracking In
description: An uppercase title converges from wide letter-spacing while its blur clears, then a subline blurs in; it exits by tracking back out into blur.
move: An uppercase title converges from wide letter-spacing while its blur clears, then a subline blurs in; it exits by tracking back out into blur.
how: A CSS variable --ls drives letter-spacing and an equal padding-left, which keeps the word optically centred at every frame (letter-spacing also trails the last glyph). --ls 0.4em→-0.03em and blur 12→0 over 1.7s with cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); opacity reaches 1 in 0.7s. Exit: --ls to 0.25em, blur 10px, fade, power2.in.
adapt: Keep the start tracking small enough that the widest frame stays inside the stage: roughly (characters × (glyph width + start tracking)) < stage width. Placeholder copy is generic; replace it with the product's words. Colours come from the palette tokens at the top of the page (--bg, --surface, --ink, --muted, --accent, --accent-2); change those to re-brand it.
port: All motion is inline in index.html. GSAP pages: register the CustomEase curves, scope selectors to the shot element and rebuild the same timeline; the split helper is inline and dependency-free.
caveats: Original implementation of the After Effects "Tracking In Long" idea; no AE preset files, expressions or numbers are copied and fidelity to a specific AE render is not claimed.
Starts and ends on an empty stage so it loops cleanly; trim the exit when the next shot cuts in.
